name: fern-minimal
why: The Artemis II relight found eighteen of nineteen beats sharing one hand-placed sun, because nothing in this repo stated the lighting rule anywhere a builder could read it. This file is that statement. It changes no shipped beat.

accent.reads_as: Kapton gold, the only warm note in a shot

palette.rule: one accent per shot, and never as the largest area

materials.rule: relief comes from raking light and real geometry, not from gloss

lighting.rule: never write a sun location as a literal; derive it from the camera at the shot's mid frame
lighting.key_side_why: key_location's side=+1 is frame-right, and tools/blender/techniques/artemis_beats.py add_key defaults to side=1.0, so every beat in the episode lights from frame-right. The archive ingest reads this one value to decide whether a clip's own light disagrees and could be mirrored; the number is not restated there.

camera.horizontal_fov_why: Derived, not invented: Blender's default camera is a 50 mm lens on a 36 mm sensor, so h_fov = 2*atan(18/50) = 39.6 degrees. An archival still declares its pan in degrees, the same unit the rate cap above is stated in, and this number is what converts those degrees into the fraction of the frame the move can actually sweep.
camera.rule: the camera may drift for the length of a sentence, never jerk

transition.rule: the cut lands on the sentence boundary, so the viewer always knows what changed

rhythm.rule: no image holds without motion or a cut for longer than ten seconds

cuts.detector: ffmpeg scdet, threshold 10, on a 320-pixel-wide copy of the master
cuts.sync_basis: 2026-11-18, ask-chatgpt v4: the detected cuts landed +0.14 s after the edit's cuts in the first 80 s and +0.65 s in the last 80 s, because every per-line segment was cut with -t and rounded to whole frames on its own. Three frames at 30 fps is the bound; the fix cuts segments by their frame position on the film clock
cuts.known_cuts_basis: 2026-11-18: the edit's own cuts come from the storyboard (tools/sound_design.py plan_events). On ask-chatgpt's first story cut the detector found 33 of 47 real cuts within 0.7 s; below 70% the rhythm reading is flagged as an undercount. Advice, not a gate: the gate keeps the detector so it stays comparable with the reference films
cuts.basis: house style — measured with this detector on six reference films (fern x3, Veritasium x3): median shot 1.48-3.25 s, 17-51% of shots under 1.5 s, longest held shot 53-228 s. The rejected ask-chatgpt cut: median 5.53 s, 7% short. Uniform pacing is a slop tell (docs/research/fern-archive-blend.md section 4); the references are bimodal, quick montage plus long explanatory moves. docs/research/story-not-slides.md

rhythm.motion_scale: mean absolute greyscale difference between frames one second apart, measured on the graded master by tools/qc_episode.py. Calibrated 2026-11-10 on all 32 Artemis II shots: the still population (both cards, both manim shots) measures 0.618-0.937 and every 3D camera move measures 1.685 or more, so 1.3 sits in the empty band between them. look_pass adds film grain, which is why a frozen frame scores 0.62 rather than 0. The slow band ends at 2.0 because the next gap in the same distribution is 1.766 to 2.580.

storyboard.why: The rejected ask-chatgpt cut put 60 pieces of text on screen in under nine minutes of 3D (30 labels, 27 HUD lines, 3 counters, 6.8 a minute) and four bar-chart beats. In the six reference films text is rare: fern shows chapter cards and the odd place or date, Veritasium a few labels inside an animation and big numbers set into footage. Charts flash for about a second (fern's Coca-Cola revenue bars: 1.0 s and 2.4 s) instead of carrying a beat. docs/research/story-not-slides.md
storyboard.text_per_minute_basis: house style — labels + HUD lines + counters per minute of 3D screen time; a third of the rejected cut's 6.8
storyboard.chart_beats_basis: house style — at most one beat in a film may be a chart; a number that matters gets a picture or a gag instead
storyboard.cut_basis: house style — the reference films are bimodal: median shot 1.3-3.2 s (montage) with held explanatory moves of 34-169 s; the rejected cut was uniform (median 5.4 s, longest 15.6 s). A storyboard needs both kinds

canvas.rule: every layer renders at this canvas; a mismatch is a silent downscale, not an error
canvas.why_this_is_the_only_source: the beats, the assembler and the rollout driver each used to type their own 1280x720, so raising one left the others downscaling it; anything that needs a canvas reads it here

audio.why_aac_384k: 2026-11-16, euv-machine: the delivery filter landed the PCM at -1.5 dBFS true peak, and ffmpeg's native aac at 192k turned one transient at 608.2 s into +1.9 dBFS, 3.4 dB of codec overshoot that no headroom can budget for. The same PCM measured -1.4 at 320k and -1.5 at 384k, and 384 kbps stereo is the AAC-LC rate YouTube recommends for upload, so the master is encoded there
audio.why_minus_9: 2026-11-16, euv-machine: a denser narration (p5 momentary -31.6 LUFS against the-light-machine's -32.8) leaves shorter gaps, and at -10 the bed lifted the floor between the words by only +1.9 dB against the 2.0 dB bound, so on a fast read it was barely there. One dB more keeps it well under the voice and audible in the gaps

ducking.basis: 2026-11-18, improvement 4 of docs/research/other-video-pipelines.md: editors duck music under dialogue (DaVinci Resolve, Audition auto-ducking). The bed is lifted 5 dB and keyed down by the narration in numpy (music_bed.duck_gain; ffmpeg's sidechaincompress gave a different file every run). Measured on ask-chatgpt, first 300 s in 100 ms windows: flat bed -35.8 dB under speech and -35.6 in pauses; ducked -36.0 under speech and -31.4 in pauses, so the words keep their distance and the pauses gain 4.2 dB

thought.why: an inner-voice line ([name:thought]) must read as inside the head, not as a second person talking: 4 dB under the levelled sentence, the top rolled off above 6 kHz (a close, soft, slightly muffled voice) and one very quiet 35 ms slap for a room around it. Subtle on purpose, the words must stay as clear as the narrator's (staging.md section 7)

sound_design.why: 2026-11-18, ask-chatgpt: the owner compared the cut with Fern and Veritasium and the track was one quiet sweep per beat change, 24 dB under the voice. The reference films lay a hit on every cut, air under every camera move, a sound on every part that switches on and a room tone for every place; tools/sound_design.py reads all of these off the storyboard
sound_design.levels_basis: house style: each sound's peak (rooms: their RMS) in dB under the voice's RMS. A 0.3 s knock at full peak carries about 12 dB less energy than its peak, so a hit 2 dB under the voice's RMS is heard about 14 LU under the voice; the first try at 15 dB put the whole effects track 28 LU under the voice, inaudible under a bed 9 LU down

reverb.basis: house style: a short synthetic room (0.7 s decay) under the hits, air and pops, so they sit in a space instead of on top of the picture; rooms stay dry. Improvement 4 of docs/research/other-video-pipelines.md

audio.rule: the platform normalises to -14 LUFS, so a quiet master is turned up by the platform and a loud one is turned down; ship at the target and the viewer hears what was mixed
audio.measured_on_artemis_ii: -25.3 LUFS integrated, -3.4 dBFS true peak, mono 24 kHz — 11.3 LU under target, which is why this section exists
audio.why_not_a_plain_gain: the measured +11.3 dB needed to reach target would have taken the -3.4 dBFS true peak to +7.9 dBFS, which clips; two-pass loudnorm with linear=true reaches the target and limits only where the ceiling demands it
audio.why_a_floor_and_not_a_loudness: a bed 10 dB under the voice moves integrated loudness by +0.07 LU on the real 470 s narration, which loudnorm then erases by landing both mixes at -14; the p5 momentary floor between the words is what survives, measured +4.2 dB with the bed and 0.0 dB without on 2026-11-12, so the bound sits between those two numbers
audio.why_the_ceiling_needs_headroom: the gate reads the peak off the encoded master. 2026-11-12: the bed mix measured -25.29 LUFS / -6.41 dBFS, the delivery filter landed the PCM at -14.00 LUFS / -1.00 dBFS (on the ceiling, zero margin), and aac -b:a 192k moved it to -0.70 dBFS, which is the breach that blocked this master (the master in work/ measured -0.60). Aiming a few tenths under the ceiling is what makes it reachable after the codec

qc.rule: an episode is finished when the gate prints no errors, not when the render exits zero

empty_shots.basis: 2026-11-18, ask-chatgpt v4, the middle frame of each of 141 shots at 320 px: median 11% of the picture carries an edge; the shots a reviewer called empty (a black screen, a phone alone in the dark, a dim screen) were 0.6-1.8%, and everything from 3% up had a subject. Advice, not a gate, until another episode calibrates it (improvement 2 of docs/research/other-video-pipelines.md)

voice.rule: one narrator voice for every episode; the API key stays in the environment, never in this file
voice.characters: characters who speak in their own voice (a `[name]` or `[name:thought]` line in narration.md) are cast per episode in script/cast.json with an installed English Kokoro voice or an ElevenLabs voice (`eleven:<voice_id>`, key in ELEVENLABS_API_KEY or the git-ignored .env.local; every line is cached in vo/eleven-cache so a re-run costs no credits); names the voice misreads are respelt for synthesis only in script/pronounce.json; every such line is declared in script/dramatisation.json (basis: verified claims, note: what is imagined)

script.words_per_second_basis: measured on the Jensen master: 444 words in 188.2 s of narration including pauses (Kokoro af_heart, speed 1)
script.rule: tools/qc_script.py runs before narration is synthesised: a script that is too short, opens slowly, has no chapters, carries a line no source stands behind, or writes numbers a voice cannot read never reaches the renderer

story.why: The owner rejected the ask-chatgpt cut as a presentation. Measured on six reference films (fern: Coca-Cola Freestyle, Secret Service, modern cars; Veritasium: fiber optics, Google Maps, jet engines; docs/research/story-not-slides.md) with the same regexes as here: they turn the story (but, problem, turns out...) 1.5-3.1 times a minute, ask 0.35-0.73 questions a minute, put numbers in 16-32% of sentences and never more than 6 numeric sentences in a row. The rejected cut: 0.9 turns, 0.27 questions, 47% numeric, a run of 10. A script reads as a fact list when numbers outrun problems.
story.numeric_sentence_share_basis: house style — the highest reference value (Google Maps, 32%)
story.numeric_run_basis: house style — reference maxima 2-6 consecutive sentences carrying a number
story.questions_per_minute_basis: house style — reference minimum 0.35 (fiber optics, Coca-Cola)
story.story_file_doc: {"question": "u006", "payoff": "u137", "follow": "cat", "guess": "u008", "reversal": "u052", "hook": {"kind": "mystery", "image": "a pulse of light filmed racing around a coil of fibre"}, "people": [{"name": "Charles Kao", "line": "u016"}]} — the open question the film owes the viewer, the line that pays it off, the wrong explanation a viewer would assume and the line that breaks it, who or what the viewer follows, and the real people whose decisions move the story
story.question_by_seconds_basis: YouTube's Intro retention segment is the first 30 s (docs/research/fern-archive-blend.md section 3)
story.people_basis: house style — every reference film moves through named people (Kao, Maurer, Keck; Dijkstra; Clint Hill; the Coca-Cola spreadsheet analyst); the rejected cut had none

hook.why: 2026-11-18, the owner: the start has to be shocking, interesting or a mystery, something that pulls the viewer in. The first 30 s are YouTube's intro retention segment (docs/research/fern-archive-blend.md section 3); the earlier opening ('You ask ChatGPT why your cat sounds like a carburettor...') was a mild scene-setter
hook.basis: house style; the gap rule reuses the turn words measured on the reference films

story.turn_basis: house style, not measured on the reference films — Derek Muller's PhD work (University of Sydney, 2008), on which Veritasium is built, found that science videos which first state the common wrong explanation and then refute it teach more than clear expositions; the second ask-chatgpt cut gave its answer in line 5 of 127, so the midpoint 'actually, no' broke nothing the viewer believed

graphics._why: Every 2D graphic (stat cards, tallies, plans, boards, labels, archive mats) draws from this one block, so a number card made for episode two is the same family as the tally made for the pilot. Sizes are fractions of frame height because the canvas is the only source of pixels; the mobile floor is the smallest a label or number may be and still read on a phone held at arm's length. An episode `look` may swap palette entries and nothing else: type, margins and motion are house rules, not episode taste.
graphics.caption_note: caption is for provenance tags only (credit, source); it matches archive.source_card.height_fraction and is the one tier allowed under the mobile floor. Anything a viewer must read is label or number.

cadence.retention_rule: retention falling inside the first minute means the hook changed, not the topic

archive.status: new visual kind — no shipped episode uses it yet; Artemis II stays as rendered
archive.rule_numbers: keys below carry the rule number from docs/research/fern-archive-blend.md section 7
archive.why: The user asked for one episode in which the 3D style and the archive-documentary style collaborate rather than alternate. The research contradicted the instinct this repo would have followed: cohesion does NOT come from pushing photographic archive into the fern-minimal grade, it comes from a shared finishing language applied to everything while each source keeps the signals of its own origin. Forcing the grade would also break the one contract rule that protects the archive's evidentiary authority.

division_of_labour.rule: the record is the archive; the animation is what the record cannot contain

animation_carries.no_camera_there: interiors and trajectories no camera had

division_of_labour.carries_rule: every archival record names the archive_carries token the shot serves; an animation_carries token is refused rather than warned about, because that is the forbidden case below stated in the file the build reads. The two lists share no token, so the answer is decidable.
division_of_labour.carries_why: Which of the two styles carries a shot was an editorial judgement nothing could check, so an episode could fill its archival layer with clips that were really an excuse not to build the shot - the one use the fair-use standard and editor craft both refuse, from opposite directions. Naming the category in the record makes the judgement legible to whoever reads the episode next, and refusing an animation-side category makes the refusal mechanical. The prose stays the contract's own wording; the token is only what a JSON file can hold without retyping a sentence into every episode.
division_of_labour.30: style-based reconstruction is what keeps an animated documentary a documentary rather than a docudrama: declared artificiality prevents the viewer mistaking recreation for footage
division_of_labour.forbidden: an archival clip used merely to avoid shooting or building the equivalent shot (fair-use standard and editor craft converge on this from opposite directions)

evidence.rule: an archival record shows one specific, named thing (a person, an event, a product model, a document, a named place) and may only play under a line that names it. A clip of 'a data centre' under a line about data centres is illustration, not evidence, and is what the owner rejected as AI slop
evidence.depicts_doc: list of the names the clip is evidence of, as the narration says them (e.g. ["Abilene"], ["GB200 NVL72"], ["Charles Kao"]); matched case-insensitively against the line text
evidence.generic_terms_why: nouns that name a category rather than a thing; a depicts list made only of these is stock footage by definition

episode_profile.why: The archival layer is part of the house style from here on, for every episode, so the obligation is stated as data the build reads rather than a habit someone has to remember. Before this block the layer was a capability an episode could fall out of without anything noticing: tools/assemble_episode.py, tools/qc_episode.py and workflow/init_episode.py each carry no reference to it, and an archive.json sitting in an episode directory was the only thing that made the layer exist.

mode_meaning.off: the mix is not judged and no finding is produced. Kept so a branch can build without the layer while testing something else; an episode may not choose it and the shipped contract never sits on it.
mode_meaning.warn: produce every finding that closed would refuse, with the same codes and the same numbers, and let the build continue. This is the rung a rollout is cut over on: the rule is measured against real distributions before it is allowed to stop a build, which is the same reason enforcement_policy keeps pixel rules on the warn side.
mode_meaning.closed: refuse the build before a single frame renders, the way a missing required capability refuses init_episode rather than warning and continuing.

mix.layers_why: the visual taxonomy as contract data. The render queue, the canvas test and the QC gate read this list, so a fifth kind becomes one edit here instead of four tuples that can quietly disagree about what the film is made of.
mix.measured_on: screen seconds summed per layer, from shots.json against the vo/manifest.json clock
mix.measured_on_basis: house style — a share in shot counts is carried by one-second inserts laid over long beats, which is the failure the reference cut-ups do not have; seconds are what the viewer actually receives

min_share.basis: house style — owner decision 2026-11-17 after the ask-chatgpt cut: a share floor made the planner fill 20% of the film with generic data-centre clips, which the owner called random and AI slop. Measured on fern and Veritasium (docs/research/story-not-slides.md): their archive is always the specific thing the line names (the real shooting, the real ad, the real Corning lab), so the amount follows the evidence there is, not a quota. No floor; archive.evidence decides which clips may appear at all

min_per_act.basis: house style — same decision: a per-act quota is the same padding pressure spread thinner

mix.act_seconds_basis: house style — an act is a three-to-five-minute span; the rhythm section bounds a single shot, not a structure, so the partition is ours
mix.act_rule: a shot belongs to the act its start falls in; the last act may run short rather than leave a tail unmetered

opt_out.effect: a valid record moves a closed episode down to warn and adds an archive_layer_opted_out finding carrying the reason, the approver and the expiry; it never removes a finding
opt_out.why: The research is blunt about how a house style dies: not by a rejected rule but by an unlogged exception. A structured reason, a named approver and an expiry are what make the opt-out reviewable by someone who was not in the room, and the downgrade-not-silence rule is what stops the exemption from also deleting the evidence.

paths.why: The archival ledger is its own file rather than another row in assets/license-manifest.json, because that file's validator in tools/sourcing/manifest.py enforces an exact thirteen-field stock schema and rejects any key it does not know. A purchase status and a rights basis are different questions: a stock asset either is bought or it is not, while an archival asset is usually free and has to say why it is free. Both validators stay exact, which is the property that catches a field renamed by accident.
paths.source_dir_rule: every archival asset lives under this directory, so a media/ folder can no longer be read as a claim that its contents are Apache-2.0

source_card.font_file_why: The same file the captions and the 3D labels load, resolved through workflow.config.resolve_path against the repo root rather than named in the ingest. A card set in a different face from the film's own titling is a second style arriving on screen for no reason, and the house font is the only thing that makes an archival credit look like it belongs to this programme rather than to the archive it came from.
source_card.text_required_why: a quotation's whole claim to be fair use is that it is subordinate and attributed, so a fair_use_quotation row with a blank credit_line cannot be drawn as a card borrowed from some other field — the ingest refuses instead of shipping a quotation with no source on screen. Other bases may hold a blank line and simply get no card.
source_card.render_measured: the card is outlined text, not a box, and the outline is what keeps it legible over any frame: tesseract reads "Apollo" back at confidence 72 from a 1080-line frame drawn at height_fraction with a stroke of 0.06 of the glyph height, and reads nothing at all from the same frame with the card removed.
source_card.in_point_rule: the card is held at the shot's in-point rather than centred, because a viewer who cannot tell where the footage came from has been shown a clip, not a source
source_card.basis: fern labels every archival insert on screen; the contract's own rights block calls the card the evidence that a quotation stays subordinate

ingest_encode.why: The ingest output is an intermediate the assembler re-encodes, so this is the one encode in the pipeline allowed to be generous: crf 17 against the beats' 18 and the master's 20, because film grain and a hard pillarbox edge are exactly what a second x264 generation eats. Declared here rather than held in the ingest's own head because it is a number that reaches the screen through two generations of compression — D-017.
ingest_encode.audio_rule: 17: no audio stream at all in an archival intermediate (the ingest passes -an), so a clip's embedded library music cannot survive into the bed the editor builds

rights.enforcement: blocking — metadata, so these are errors, not advisories
rights.field_types_why: A blank string is not the only way a field goes undocumented, and for the structured half of the row it is not even the common way. An empty obligations list reads to a human as 'no obligations' and to a `.strip()` check as a filled cell; a qc_watermark of false is the answer that makes shipping a watermarked master impossible and would be deleted by that same check; a timebase of '24' passes it and then compares as text, which gates nothing. So each field declares the kind of answer that counts as an answer, and the validator refuses a value of the wrong kind by name.
rights.unresolved_placeholders_why: 'unknown' in a rights field is the spreadsheet export that shipped. It satisfies a presence check, prints a blank in the on-screen card, and tells the next reader that somebody looked and could not tell — which is a different fact from never having looked, and the one an orphan-works argument cannot survive. Compared after stripping spaces, hyphens and underscores and casefolding, so 'Not Known' variants are not a separate list. Not applied to third_party_rights, which has its own closed rule: there 'none' is a real answer while here it is a gap.
rights.third_party_rights_rule: an agency's clearance answers only for the agency. Music, faces, trademarks and contractor material inside federal footage are separately encumbered, so the field is either an explicit 'none' or a list of what else is in the frame. 'unknown' is refused rather than warned about: a rights-unknown row is a stop, and the research found no body that treats it as a to-do.
rights.obligations_required_for_bases_why: These four bases grant use only on terms — attribution, share-alike, a paid clause, or the subordination argument. Recording the licence and not the duty is how a compliant file gets published non-compliantly. cc0, pd_expired and us_federal_public_domain impose nothing, so there an empty list stays a true statement.
rights.quotation_ceiling_rule: fair_use_quotation_max_seconds is measured on the real seconds between in_timecode and out_timecode, not on the labels: a drop-frame span and a non-drop span of the same written length differ by two frames a minute, and a ceiling applied to the label over-grants the time nobody recorded.
rights.publication_year_floor_basis: house style pending confirmation — derived from the 95-year term, which puts works published in or before 1930 in the US public domain as of 2026. The research flagged it as needing a Copyright Office confirmation before it decides a ship, so this number gates pd_expired claims on an unconfirmed reading of US law until that check is on record.
rights.drop_frame_rule: SMPTE drop-frame notation exists only for the 1.001 ratios. It skips frame numbers so the label keeps telling clock time, which means the label is not a frame count: 00:01:00;00 names the 1798th frame, while 00:01:00:00 names the 1800th. timebase and source_frame_rate stay separate fields because the first is the label's modulus and the second is what the tape actually ran at.
rights.credential_query_rule: a ledger URL is published text — it reaches the description block and sometimes the screen. A source link carrying an access credential leaks the credential into a shipped artefact, so the ledger refuses one. Underscores and hyphens are ignored when matching, and the names live here as data so the validator that enforces them contains no credential-shaped literal of its own.
rights.source_concentration_max_share_basis: house style — distilled from rule 22 of docs/research/fern-archive-blend.md, 'do not rely disproportionately on one source'; no archive or documentation body publishes a concentration cap, so the number is this repo's taste
rights.fair_use_quotation_max_seconds_basis: house style — a quotation ceiling in seconds is a legal argument a human makes, not a published threshold; the number is what this repo will not ship without a stated purpose
rights.attribution_window_seconds_basis: house style — the requirement is that narration names or analyses the source near its in-point; 8 s is how close this repo calls near
rights.fair_use_quotation_requires: narration within attribution_window_seconds of the in-point names the source or analyses it — quotation must be subordinate to the larger intellectual purpose
rights.source_card_owner: archive.source_card owns the on-screen card: whether it appears, which ledger field supplies its text, how long it holds and where it sits. Stated here because the rule belongs to the rights, enforced there so the ingest and the gate read one block rather than agreeing twice.
rights.description_block: every archival clip with timecode, source, rights basis and licence link
rights.insignia_rule: agency logos and identifiers are not public domain even when the footage is, and NASA asks that its insignia not appear alongside AI-generated imagery — this repo's 3D is human-made, declared so, but a composite that puts the insignia on synthetic material is still refused
rights.archive_rights_statement_rule: an Internet Archive rights statement describes the item, it does not grant permission; the licence is established from the item's own metadata or the holding institution
rights.media_folder_rule_change: media/ no longer means Apache-2.0-only. It means: an asset either is owned by the project or is archival with a documented rights_basis row in the licence ledger. PRODUCTION-GUIDE section 5 carries the prose

sourcing.why: The archival layer is the house default, so finding the footage has to be the house default too. Every number, endpoint, field name and refusal reason an archiver needs is stated here rather than in tools/, because a policy that lives in code is a policy one episode can carry and the next cannot — the same reason #146 deleted the assembler's shot table. Nothing in this block needs a credential: anonymous read is enough on all three hosts, and a code path that can carry a key is the failure being avoided, not the key itself.
sourcing.report_filename_why: the accepted/refused split with each refusal's searched field paths is evidence, not a gate. It is deliberately not the ledger and not archive.json: a candidate refused for lack of evidence must leave a record of the search without ever reaching #148's round-trip check.
sourcing.user_agent_why: Commons answers 403 to a request with no User-Agent, so the header is transport, not a courtesy; and archive.org's bots guidance asks for a project URL in it.
refuse_before_download_when: no archive shot on the timeline
sourcing.refuse_why: D-043. A partial ledger is worse than no ledger: it validates, it fills the layer's share, and it says nothing about the shots it could not place.

transport.policy: 429 and 503 wait; a Retry-After header overrides the ladder; 403 is a client bug (on Commons it is a missing User-Agent) and waiting will not fix it; 400 and 404 are our request being wrong about an API that changed, which is the class that never improves on the fifth try. Exhausting the attempts is a transport failure that refuses the item as source_unavailable — it is never read as a rights verdict in either direction.
transport.sidecar_why: the ledger has to record the bytes that landed, not the bytes the provider advertised. The digest is computed while writing anyway; returning it and parking it beside the file is what lets the ingest re-read it and refuse an item that changed underneath the run.
transport.cache_why: keyed by host, url and the date of the run so an overnight re-run of the same topic costs no network and no rate-limit goodwill, and so the ledger can cite the exact raw response it decided on. A cache that crossed retrieval dates would let a rights verdict be re-issued under yesterday's evidence, and a public-domain claim is only true as of a day.

record_id.why: continues from the highest id already in the ledger, so a second run on the same episode extends it instead of renumbering rows the timeline already cites

usage.why: the span the ledger documents is the span of the source we intend to use, so it has to be stated before anyone cuts; it is capped by the duration the file actually probes at
usage.motion_mode_why: 8 mm ran at 16-18 fps and a canvas at 24-30 will make it crawl unless the retime is declared; the enum is the contract's own, so this only picks which member applies
usage.aspect_why: an archival 4:3 frame on a widescreen canvas is pillarboxed with the edge left visible, which is the honest presentation; the third state the contract rejects is an accidental crop of that edge
usage.treatment_why: cohesion comes from a shared finishing language, not from pushing photographic archive into the synthetic grade; each source keeps the signals of its own origin

transformations.pillarbox_visible_edge: pillarbox to preserve the frame edge
transformations.keep_distinct: graded to the house finish without conforming the frame

usage.defaults_why: nothing accepted here is a watermarked preview — the accepted bases are all free-of-charge — and a third-party claim inside the frame is a clearance the archiver cannot make from metadata, so it is stated as none only where the provider's own evidence says so and the rc_ hint is annotated, never gated

purpose.template: archival evidence for {slug}: {purpose_source}; the record is the archive and the animation is what the record cannot contain
purpose.override: an explicit --purpose wins, and it is the only way an editorial argument reaches the row
purpose.why: purpose_of_use is the one rights field that is an editorial claim rather than a provider fact. Inventing it would be a placeholder with a sentence around it, so the tool states what it actually knows — which film, which shot, whose record — and says plainly that the argument is not yet made.

evidence_fields.note: the machine token ExtMetadata2JSON derives from the licence template — pd, cc0, cc-by-sa-4.0. It is the only field that does not depend on a human typing a string correctly, so it decides first.
a human label like 'Public domain'. Fallback only.
free text from the description page. Fallback only, and never the primary.

contradictions.why: a PD claim against Copyrighted=Yes is two statements by the same archive about the same file; the archiver does not pick a favourite, it stops and names both fields

restrictions_gate.why: the lawful-but-awful case a documentary gets complained about: a present-and-non-empty Restrictions blocks an auto-pass even when the licence token reads pd

cc_by: attribution on screen in the source card and in the description block
cc_by_sa: attribution on screen in the source card and in the description block
share-alike: the derived work is published under the same licence

evidence_fields.note: the IA schema's own home for a licence URI, and the only one of the three that can carry a permission
typed as a free string; it holds rightsstatements URIs in real records and '(not assigned)' in others, so it is read but never trusted alone
information relevant to copyright status — prose, not a licence, and the schema says explicitly not to use it for CC

gates.label: metadata.access-restricted-item
gates.why: a lending-restricted item cannot be downloaded anonymously at all, whatever its copyright says

gates.label: geo_restricted
gates.why: restriction by territory is not a licence we can grant ourselves

cc_by: attribution on screen in the source card and in the description block
cc_by_sa: attribution on screen in the source card and in the description block
share-alike: the derived work is published under the same licence

evidence_fields.note: NASA publishes no rights field — the usage filter the old code assumed does not exist, and a query parameter cannot answer a legal question. The record is the item's own identifier under the agency that made it.

accept_from_source.why: works of the United States Government are not subject to copyright under 17 USC 105, so the basis comes from who made the item, not from a field the uploader filled in

gates.why: agency logos and identifiers are not public domain even when the footage is, and the contract's insignia_rule refuses a composite that puts them on synthetic material — this check belongs beside the rule, not in a query parameter that returns HTTP 400

hints.why: an rc_ code is a hint that third-party clearance may be outstanding. It is recorded in the evidence and annotated in the report; it never gates, because gating on a hint would be the same invention the old usage filter was

refusal_reasons.no_recognized_basis: no priority field carried a value any rule recognizes — the report names every field path searched
refusal_reasons.noncommercial: an NC licence cannot serve a monetized documentary
refusal_reasons.no_derivatives: the layer pillarboxes, grades and crops; an ND licence forbids exactly that
refusal_reasons.rights_statement_only: a rightsstatements.org URI is a claim about a claim, not a grant; refused unless a licence URI is present to decide
refusal_reasons.access_restricted: the item is not obtainable anonymously
refusal_reasons.geo_restricted: the item is unplayable from this territory
refusal_reasons.copyrighted_contradicts_pd: two fields of the same archive disagree about the same file
refusal_reasons.restrictions_present: a Restrictions claim sits on top of the licence
refusal_reasons.insignia_present: the agency's own identifiers are outside the grant
refusal_reasons.missing_field: a field the ledger requires is one this provider cannot supply — the field is named, never padded
refusal_reasons.publication_year_floor: a pd_expired claim whose source_year has not run its term
refusal_reasons.source_unavailable: the transport failed after the declared attempts; a network fault is never read as a rights verdict
refusal_reasons.request_shape: the payload came back empty in a way that means our query was wrong, not that no footage exists — reported apart from a rights verdict, because collapsing the two is how a typo silences a corpus

cohesion.default_why: photographic archive keeps its aspect ratio, frame edge, dust and original contrast because those signal provenance; blend is reserved for material already degraded (surveillance, low-bitrate web transfers) where a faithful grade would misrepresent its origin anyway
cohesion.shared_finishing_pass: tools/look_pass.py, invoked once on the assembled master after concat — grain, bloom, vignette and contrast reach every source in one transform, which is the mechanism the research says carries cohesion
cohesion.shared_finishing_pass_rule: 7: a second grade pass, or a per-shot grain injection outside look_pass, breaks the single-transform claim the gate asserts

finish.strengths_why: These are the values that survived looking at them: contrast past ~1.03 or a vignette past ~0.30 swallowed the shadow side of the capsule whole, and the shadow side is the half the narration is usually describing. They lived as Python defaults in tools/look_pass.py, which made the one transform every source shares the only place in the pipeline where a number reaching the screen was not contract data (D-017). An episode cannot now carry a different grade than the house one, and a look-dev override is recorded as an override rather than becoming the next default by accident.
finish.encode_why: The grade is the last picture encode before the mux, which copies the stream, so crf 19 sits between the beats' 18 and the archival ingest's 17: generous enough that grain survives it, tight enough that the grain it adds is the grain that ships.
finish.order_rule: grade, bloom, sharpen, grain, vignette - and the order is load-bearing rather than stylistic. Sharpen before grain, never after, or the unsharp mask lifts the noise it just made and the shot sparkles. Vignette last, because anything after it re-lights the corners. An element declared 0 leaves the graph instead of sitting in it at zero strength.
finish.report_filename_why: The single-transform claim is only checkable if the run says what it did: the strengths it used, the filtergraph it built, the digest of the file it wrote, and whether any strength was overridden away from the contract. The gate reads this file rather than trusting that look_pass ran, which is the same reason the archival report is evidence and the ledger is not.

cohesion.matching_order_rule: colour cannot fix a bad cut and texture comes last; fix the single most visible difference first
cohesion.noise_before_grain: 10: match residual noise to the episode band before look_pass adds designed grain; a too-clean archival insert reads digital next to film grain

light_direction.rule: the 3D key is derived from the camera (lighting.key_yaw_deg -15, key_elevation_deg 17); the archive never controls its light, so this is the cheapest cohesion lever available and the only one the ingest can act on
light_direction.mirror_guard: an archival frame may be horizontally flipped to agree with the 3D key only if OCR finds no readable text in it — mirroring evidence that carries writing, a plaque, a caption or a instrument panel is falsification
light_direction.capability_required_why: the id in workflow/capabilities.json whose executable check carries Tesseract — not the binary name, because tesseract is not on PATH here and only the registry knows where it lives. The ingest resolves its scanner through that same entry, so the gate and the code it gates can never disagree about whether this machine can read text.

cohesion.blend_luma_applies_to: blend shots only; keep_distinct shots are exempt by design
cohesion.archival_audio_rule: 17: strip stock-embedded music, rebuild the ambience from the film's own palette, and hold any source music 10 dB under the voice — the same offset as the bed

archive_motion.form_why: a clip has a frame rate to reinterpret and a still does not; the two share every other rule, so the enum lives beside the rate rules that read it
archive_motion.motion_mode_required_when: native fps is not the canvas fps
archive_motion.why: Standard 8 runs near 16 fps and Super 8 near 18; played at 30 that is the comic fast-walk tell. Either retime to natural motion or keep period motion and let it read as period — undeclared is the only failure
archive_motion.still_move_requires: both a pan and a scale change, terminating rather than looping
archive_motion.why_stills_move: a still gets screen time instead of sitting dead on the timeline; this is also what the existing motion gate demands of a card, and the reason the assembler rejects a still card

archive_aspect.bar_colour_why: Declared, not defaulted. Measured: an undeclared pad on yuv420p lands at 0/0/0 on this build, and the graded master's own vignette corners reach 0 too, so black is both the encoder default and the episode's floor — which is exactly why the value still belongs here rather than in the encoder's head. D-017's rule is that any number reaching the screen is contract data, and this filter's chroma handling for YUV has changed between ffmpeg versions before.
archive_aspect.why: 4:3 inside 16:9 keeps its frame edge visible because the shape signals provenance. designed_container is the diegetic upgrade — the old footage projected onto an object that references the period. A third state, an accidental edge crop of the 4:3 frame, is rejected
archive_aspect.resize_to_full_frame_requires: a pan that was not in the original, declared as our move rather than presented as the source's

archive_rhythm.archival_share_status: internal cap, unvalidated — no source supports a per-minute figure and the research rejects formulas; this is ours until retention data says otherwise
archive_rhythm.max_archival_shot_basis: 13: the two-four-six second test — keep the shortest version that conveys the information. Anything past six seconds must survive the removal test: mute it and cut it, and if nothing is lost it was padding
archive_rhythm.cut_on_meaning: the cut lands on a change in meaning (new noun, verb, place, memory, consequence, question), not on a beat
archive_rhythm.audio_bridge: L-cut and J-cut carry the viewer across a source change; lower the music at the transition, never the narration

hook.measure_at_basis: 19: YouTube defines its Intro retention segment as the percentage still watching after the first 30 seconds — that is the boundary to score against, not a guessed timestamp. The existing rhythm.hook_max_seconds 10 stays as the stricter internal ceiling
hook.opens_a_loop: the first two sentences contain at least one of: interrogative, unresolved referent, negation-open, withheld-evidence cue
hook.enigma_box: build a puzzle, not an action; describe what the thing is not; widen the gap explicitly when the evidence is withheld
hook.payoff: promise a worthy payoff and keep it
hook.not_a_context_dump: front-loaded context causes cognitive overload; intrigue, do not confuse

slop_guards.provenance_declaration: the episode states that its visuals combine human-made animation and third-party archive, and the source cards mark which is which. fern opens every video with the line that its animations are made by real humans — a values claim, not a production claim
slop_guards.garbled_text_guard: 21: OCR the renders and any restyled in-image text; a token outside the episode's expected-text dictionary is the 'expror' tell
slop_guards.framing_variance: 22: at least 4 distinct framings per scene, and no 3 consecutive shots sharing a framing-and-palette signature
slop_guards.no_uniform_pacing: 14: a shot-duration distribution with coefficient of variation under 0.25 is the uniform 3-4 second rhythm the slop taxonomy names
slop_guards.no_synthetic_looking_archival: 16: an archival-look detector (heavy desaturation or sepia plus strong vignette plus film grain plus gate weave plus 4:3 edge) fires on 0 percent of 3D and Manim shots — the machine-checkable form of never letting recreation pass as original footage
slop_guards.no_silent_template_reuse: 23: two beats sharing a motion template must differ in parameter hash
slop_guards.voice: no robotic flat VO — pitch variation and emphasis pauses; an ambient bed under the narration is mandatory, which is what the music-floor gate already measures
slop_guards.resolution: 720p or below is a slop marker; this repo ships 1920x1080

enforcement_policy.metadata_rules: error — deterministic and cheap to satisfy, so they block the build
enforcement_policy.pixel_rules: warn until measured — a bound taken from a vendor checklist or a forum rather than from our own frames ships false positives, and a gate that blocks on an uncalibrated number gets bypassed. Promote to error only with the measured distribution in the finding text, the way rhythm.motion_static_max was placed in the empty band between 0.937 and 1.685
enforcement_policy.calibration_owner: the first episode that carries archival shots produces the distributions these bounds are set from
